findings.summary: The fallback c45 citation cites lines that do not say Queued, so the real source check may flag c45, fail criterion 3's 'source check passes', and queue a c45 fix request on the first drain.
findings.evidence: claims.json:346 c45 text says 'the backlog row goes back to Queued'. The fallback quotes are claims.json:169 ('replaced by `tasks-axi reopen`') and :180 ('reopens the row instead of closing it'); neither mentions Queued. Glob finds no fm-teardown.sh or pinned-source/ in this copy. The reading allows this route if the CHANGELOG says what was not checked. Fix: Have the CHANGELOG and the job outcome say that criterion 3's source-check half is expected to fail on c45 until it is re-cited from the mounted pin, and that one c45 fix request will likely be queued by the next drain. If the producer has the pinned tree, prefer finding the exact Queued line there.

findings.summary: When model.json fails its own consistency check (the floor), check_page returns early and queues no fix request. The plan neither states nor documents this.
findings.evidence: drain.rs:4696-4698 returns Check::fail(problems) before the source-check loop, so report.findings is never produced for those failures. Fix: State in the module doc and CHANGELOG that only source-check findings are queued and model self-consistency failures still only hold the page back. Or say explicitly that this is out of scope.

findings.summary: Test 7 would pass without the new code: guarded already deletes a stale carry, and the fixture directory has never been queued in this process, so check_page queues one request either way.
findings.evidence: guarded (drain.rs:3854-3860) already removes carry_file when not carried over; the fresh fixture's directory has no entry in the static. Fix: Keep it as a regression test, but strengthen it: put the same marker in the static under a different directory first, showing that only a same-directory marker suppresses queueing. Or drop the claim that it shows new behavior.

summary: Round 4 answers the earlier findings. The run-scoped marker set now survives the rebuild re-exec through the existing drain.carry file. I checked in drain.rs: Carried (3219) derives Default and serde; run_pass (3303-3322) takes the carry before pass() and stores it only when a restart is due; guarded (3842-3860) removes a carry unless this drain is continuing after its own rebuild. commands.rs:341-357 builds a new RealSteps per pass, which confirms a static alone would not survive the rebuild. Matching that picks the owning study entry is now one-way with a half-length rule, so a short unrelated definition no longer claims a long statement. The names the plan cites exist: StewardRequest::new (steward.rs:535, title reworded), plain_boundary_text, structural_pass_open (code_health.rs:573), request_jobs, looks_like_path and the OutcomeState variants. Each demonstration names a real production seam (check_page, queue, run_pass, guarded with a real carry file) and would fail without its behavior: a key of file and kind only fails run 3, open-only dedup fails test 2, a missing carry field fails tests 5 and 6. The dependents list covers the readers I grepped. Remaining issues are minor. The fallback c45 citation will likely make the real source check flag c45, so criterion 3's pass half is expected to fail until the pinned source is mounted; the reading allows this route. The model self-consistency failures return early and queue nothing, which the plan does not state. The stale-carry test re-tests existing guarded behavior and would pass without the new code.
